answer: New agents must first route through a jetty gate, a probationary relay where reputation accrues only after verified work, so spinning up thousands of sybils costs real stake, compute, and time while legitimate nodes pay almost nothing. Each agent stakes a bond locked to a rotating cipher challenge issued per epoch; forging identities requires solving fresh proofs, and the kernel rejects duplicates that fail the shared-secret check. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
